title: From AI mockup to usable wireframe
goal: Turn an image concept into a labelled, testable interface plan.
explanation: An attractive image is not a working app, and image-generated text is often unreliable. Start with a single user task and a content hierarchy. Use an image generator optionally for visual exploration, then redraw the actual labels and focus order in a simple document or design tool.
sampleInput: Fictional task: a beginner wants to log a ten-minute walk. Screen needs: activity name, duration, save action, cancel action and a confirmation/error state. No calorie estimate, health claim, account details or personal location is needed.
prompt: Propose a mobile wireframe for logging a walk. Put the task title first, labelled duration field second, primary Save activity action third and a secondary Cancel action nearby. Specify empty, invalid and success states in text. If creating an image, use placeholder blocks, not claims that the rendered text or interface is accessible.
workedExample: A usable specification says: duration accepts a positive number of minutes; blank shows “Enter a duration”; zero shows “Use more than zero minutes”; success says “Walk saved: 10 minutes.” A pretty image with an unlabeled number field fails.

steps.title: Define the task
steps.text: Write what the person must complete in one sentence and remove unrelated features.

steps.title: Explore one concept
steps.text: Generate a layout description or optional image; keep it labelled as a concept.

steps.title: Make a real wireframe
steps.text: Replace image text with editable labels and write each control’s purpose.

steps.title: Walk through failures
steps.text: Try blank, zero and valid duration on paper; map the exact messages and next actions.

steps.title: Test with a reader
steps.text: Ask someone to identify the primary action and explain what happens next without your coaching.

checks: Every field has an explicit editable label and a described purpose.
Empty, invalid and success states are specified, not merely drawn.
The report calls the image a mockup, not a functional or accessibility-certified interface.
commonMistakes: Judging usability from visual polish alone.
Assuming dark mode or high contrast guarantees accessibility.
offline: Draw a labelled paper wireframe and run the same three-state walkthrough with a reader.

visualSteps.title: Test
visualSteps.text: Ask a reader to walk through

reflection: Which missing state did the image fail to show?

evidence.title: Keep the build
evidence.detail: Save your original input, exact prompt and resulting artifact. Every field has an explicit editable label and a described purpose.

evidence.title: Show what you tested
evidence.detail: Record a pass/fail result and evidence for every check below. Empty, invalid and success states are specified, not merely drawn.

evidence.title: Explain a limitation
evidence.detail: Write what changed after one deliberate revision and name a remaining failure mode. Judging usability from visual polish alone.

editorialStatus: Original authored activity; independent subject-matter review and learner timing remain pending.
